method.moon_routes: straight lines on the region's 30 m tile (moon/<id>.bin), 1/1.5/2 km, 16 directions, starts every 750 m; gentle = 10th, steeper = 60th percentile of mean |slope| over all tile routes
method.dtw: banded DTW (Sakoe-Chiba radius 10 % = 10 samples) on 100-point signed slope profiles, |a-b| cost normalised by warping-path length (deg)
method.candidates: Calgary walks with length 0.6-1.6x the Moon route
method.tie_break: among walks within 10 % (+0.05 deg) of the best DTW, prefer tracts in the Highest/High Accessibility & Amenities category (greatest need; City: 'When interpreting the total equity score and domain scores, a higher score means greater inequities and needs and more barriers to equity', https://www.calgary.ca/research/calgary-equity-index.html), then a start within 400 m of an ACTIVE stop, then the nearer stop

notes: Moon south-pole terrain is mostly steeper than city paths: the 9 Artemis III candidate regions have median slopes of roughly 7-18 deg at 30 m, while City of Calgary pathways rarely exceed ~5 deg over a 30 m step. Calgary walks reproduce the gentler traverse segments of a Moon route (the rhythm of climbs and descents), not the hazard itself. They are for outreach and education, not mission or equipment testing. Profiles come from the NRCan 2020 lidar bare-earth DTM read at 4 m; pathways on bridges and overpasses are bridged by interpolation (bridge_repaired). Transit and Equity Index fields are context for choosing where to run public walks; they are not accessibility certifications. Equity Index direction: the City states "When interpreting the total equity score and domain scores, a higher score means greater inequities and needs and more barriers to equity" (https://www.calgary.ca/research/calgary-equity-index.html); access_domain_score and access_category therefore measure NEED (Highest = greatest barriers), and the preset tie-break favours Highest/High tracts. In the 2024 data this domain is anti-correlated with the index's Transit Score (Spearman -0.83) and Walk Score (-0.88): the highest-need tracts for access & amenities are mostly newer outer suburbs with weak transit and walkability.
